title: CSG operations do not respect the "top_level" flag of the node's transform
body: ### Tested versions Tested in 4.6.1 ### System information Godot v4.6.1.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 (NVIDIA; 27.21.14.5751) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-9100F CPU @ 3.60GHz (4 threads) - 15.91 GiB memory ### Issue description When the "top_level" flag (Node3D) of a CSG node is set to true, boolean operations involving the node still assume the node's transform is relative to it's parent transform, such that the effect of the boolean operation becomes displaced from the node responsible for it. The expected behavior is that the effect of the boolean operation should remain consistent with where the node is physically located in the scene, rather than being displaced. ### Steps to reproduce 1. In a 3D scene, create a CSGBox3D node and form it into a "wall" along the x-axis. 2. Translate the wall node some short distance along the x-axis. 3. Create another CSGBox3D as a child of the wall and set it's operation to "Subtraction". Make sure it penetrates the wall to form a visible hole. 4. In the inspector for the subtraction node, under "Node3D", set the "Top Level" flag to true. The hole in the wall should now be displaced from the subtraction node. Top Level = False Top Level = True ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [CSG_TopLevel_MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26125545/CSG_TopLevel_MRP.zip)
